events.title: Bush carries Nevada
events.text: George W. Bush carried Nevada by three and a half points; since 1912 it has backed the national winner in all but two elections.

events.title: Guinn re-elected
events.text: Governor Kenny Guinn, a Republican, won a second term with 68 percent.

events.title: Bush again
events.text: Bush carried Nevada a second time, by under three points.

events.title: Gibbons elected
events.text: Jim Gibbons, a Republican, beat Dina Titus by four points.

events.title: Shortage rules
events.text: The federal government set the Colorado River shortage guidelines that still govern Lake Mead.

events.title: Culinary backs Obama
events.text: The Culinary Union, Las Vegas's largest union, endorsed Barack Obama before the caucuses.

events.title: Obama by 12.5
events.text: Barack Obama carried Nevada by twelve and a half points, its widest Democratic margin of the period.

events.title: Sandoval elected
events.text: Brian Sandoval beat Rory Reid by almost twelve points; Governor Gibbons had lost the Republican primary.

events.title: Obama again
events.text: Obama carried Nevada by almost seven points.

events.title: Sandoval re-elected
events.text: Sandoval won a second term with almost 71 percent of the vote.

events.title: Sheriff Lombardo
events.text: Joe Lombardo was elected sheriff of Clark County, head of the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police.

events.title: Third intake
events.text: A third intake began drawing Las Vegas's water from deeper in Lake Mead.

events.title: A bellwether misses
events.text: Nevada voted for Hillary Clinton, one of only two times since 1912 it backed the national loser.

events.title: Sisolak elected
events.text: Steve Sisolak beat Adam Laxalt, the first Democrat elected governor since 1994.

events.title: Ford elected AG
events.text: Aaron Ford, the state Senate majority leader, was elected attorney general, the first African American elected to statewide constitutional office in Nevada.

events.title: Automatic registration
events.text: Voters approved automatic registration at the DMV; it began in 2020.

events.title: Unemployment 30%
events.text: With the casinos closed, Nevada's unemployment reached 30.5 percent in April, by the revised count.

events.title: Biden by 2.4
events.text: Joe Biden carried Nevada by 33,596 votes.

events.title: Arizona flips
events.text: Arizona voted Democratic for president by three-tenths of a point.

events.title: Mail ballots for all
events.text: A state law made mail ballots for every active voter permanent.

events.title: Turf law
events.text: A state law banned Colorado River water for ornamental grass from 2027.

events.title: Lake Mead record low
events.text: Lake Mead fell to 1,040.6 feet, then a record low.

events.title: Lombardo wins
events.text: Lombardo beat Governor Sisolak by 15,386 votes; Sisolak was the only incumbent governor to lose that year.

events.title: Nonpartisans lead
events.text: Nonpartisan voters became Nevada's largest registration group.

events.title: Seventy-five vetoes
events.text: Lombardo vetoed seventy-five bills from the Democratic legislature, a single-session record.

events.title: Ethics finding
events.text: The Ethics Commission fined Lombardo $20,000 over campaign use of his sheriff's badge; in 2025 a settlement cut it to $5,000.

events.title: Electors indicted
events.text: Ford's office obtained indictments of six Republicans who signed alternate 2020 elector certificates.

events.title: “None” wins
events.text: In the Republican presidential primary, “None of these candidates” beat Nikki Haley, 63 to 31 percent.

events.title: Trump carries Nevada
events.text: Trump won Nevada by 3.1 points, the first Republican to do so since 2004.

events.title: Washoe splits
events.text: Kamala Harris carried Washoe County by 2,628 votes as Trump won the state.

events.title: Eighty-seven vetoes
events.text: Lombardo vetoed eighty-seven bills, breaking his own record.

events.title: Fewer visitors
events.text: Las Vegas drew 38.5 million visitors, down 7.5 percent from 2024.

events.title: Trump endorses Lombardo
events.text: On 7 November President Trump endorsed Lombardo for a second term.

events.title: Nevada's gold
events.text: Nevada produced about 64 percent of U.S. gold, much of it around Elko.

events.title: Culinary backs Ford
events.text: On 18 May the Culinary Union endorsed Aaron Ford.

events.title: Primary day
events.text: On 9 June Lombardo and Ford won their party primaries; Ford beat Alexis Hill, the Washoe County Commission chair.

events.title: Lake Mead record low
events.text: In August Lake Mead fell below its 2022 record low.

events.title: Colorado River cuts
events.text: Interior set 2027 cuts after the seven states failed to agree; Nevada's share is 50,000 acre-feet.

events.title: Thacker Pass
events.text: Building continued at the Thacker Pass lithium mine in Humboldt County, backed by a federal loan.

events.title: An empty podium
events.text: On 8 October Ford appeared alone at a Carson City forum that Lombardo declined.

events.title: Early voting
events.text: In-person early voting runs from 17 to 30 October; mail ballots go to every active voter.

events.title: Election Day
events.text: On 3 November Nevadans choose between Lombardo, Aaron Ford, Danielle Ford and “None of these candidates”.

eras: Sisolak, the pandemic and mail ballots
Lombardo, vetoes and a close race
chartNote: Each state is coloured by the margin of the most recent presidential popular vote (Democratic minus Republican share of all votes; certified state results). It is a simplification: Nevada chooses its governor in its own race, and Nevadans split their tickets (in 2022 a Republican won the governorship while Democrats won the Senate seat), so the presidential colour is a backdrop, not a forecast. Shares are of land area, not of people or votes: most of Nevada's land is rural, while about two-thirds of its votes are cast in Clark County. Boundaries are today's states (Natural Earth); the map is framed on Nevada, so outer states are cut at the edge.
